items.title: Remote Sensing and Image Interpretation (7th ed.)
items.authors: Thomas M. Lillesand, Ralph W. Kiefer, Jonathan W. Chipman
items.why: A standard introductory text covering sensors, image interpretation and digital image analysis, including classification.

items.title: Assessing the Accuracy of Remotely Sensed Data: Principles and Practices (3rd ed.)
items.why: The reference on error matrices, reference data collection and thematic map accuracy assessment.

items.title: Geocomputation with Python
items.authors: Michael Dorman, Anita Graser, Jakub Nowosad, Robin Lovelace
items.why: Hands-on vector and raster GIS in Python (geopandas, rasterio): the practical base for the code in this site.

items.title: Geocomputation with R
items.authors: Robin Lovelace, Jakub Nowosad, Jannes Muenchow
items.why: The R sister book; includes spatial cross-validation and statistical learning with geographic data.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning
items.why: Clear chapters on Shapley values, SHAP and permutation importance, with honest discussion of their limits.

items.title: A Land Use and Land Cover Classification System for Use with Remote Sensor Data (USGS Professional Paper 964)
items.authors: James R. Anderson, Ernest E. Hardy, John T. Roach, Richard E. Witmer
items.why: The classic hierarchical LULC scheme (Level I/II classes) that many class legends still echo.

items.title: Sentinel-2 mission (SentiWiki)
items.why: Official band, resolution and product-level reference for Sentinel-2 MSI.

items.title: Copernicus DEM
items.why: Global elevation model for deriving elevation, slope and aspect features.

items.title: WorldPop
items.why: Gridded population data used as a socio-demographic covariate.

items.title: SHAP documentation
items.why: API reference and examples for TreeExplainer and summary plots.

items.title: LightGBM documentation
items.why: Parameter guide (num_leaves, learning_rate, etc.) for tuning.

items.title: rasterio documentation
items.why: Reading, writing and windowing GeoTIFF rasters in Python.
